data.name: SettingsWindow.Text29
data.value: Step 1: Prepare Google (checked against official documentation on 2026-10-06) For personal use with your own Google account. Buttons open your default browser. Keep the same project selected throughout 1-1 to 1-5. Labels depend on Google's display language.

data.name: SettingsWindow.Text30
data.value: 1-1. Open Google Calendar API

data.name: SettingsWindow.Text31
data.value: Select a project at the top, or use New project to create and select one (e.g. StickyNotes Personal). On the Google Calendar API page, click Enable. Manage means it is already enabled.

data.name: SettingsWindow.Text32
data.value: 1-2. Open Branding

data.name: SettingsWindow.Text33
data.value: If not configured, choose Get started. • App name: e.g. StickyNotes Personal • User support email: an address you can receive → Next • Audience: External for personal Google accounts → Next • Contact information: your email → Next • Review the user-data policy and agree if appropriate → Continue → Create If already configured, review it and continue to 1-3. Internal restricts access to your Google Cloud organization.

data.name: SettingsWindow.Text34
data.value: 1-3. Open Audience

data.name: SettingsWindow.Text35
data.value: For External apps in Testing, use Test users → Add users, enter the Google account that will access the calendar, and Save. If your Cloud administration account differs, add the calendar account. You do not need to publish the app.

data.name: SettingsWindow.Text36
data.value: 1-4. Open Data Access

data.name: SettingsWindow.Text37
data.value: For an external app, choose Add or Remove Scopes and select both scopes below. If missing, enter each URL under Manually add scopes. Choose Update, then Save.

data.name: SettingsWindow.Text38
data.value: You can select and copy the URLs above. calendar.events permits viewing/editing events; tasks.readonly only permits reading Tasks. Calendar ID does not restrict the OAuth grant or select task lists.

data.name: SettingsWindow.Text39
data.value: 1-5. Open Clients

data.name: SettingsWindow.Text40
data.value: Choose Create client → Application type: Desktop app → name (e.g. StickyNotes Desktop) → Create. Use Download JSON in the result before closing it; the secret may not be retrievable later. Do not configure web-app redirect URIs or JavaScript origins. Select the downloaded JSON in Step 2, then Import into app to copy it to app data. Renaming is unnecessary. API keys and service-account JSON are not supported.

data.name: SettingsWindow.Text41
data.value: Next: Select JSON → Import into app → Calendar ID: primary for your main calendar → Step 3 to sign in. In the browser, choose the account from 1-3, verify the app name, and allow Calendar access and Tasks read access. The app receives the result automatically. Close the tab and check for Connection verified in Settings. Google Tasks is read-only. The Google Tasks API provides dates only; it cannot return scheduled times. Even when a time is set in Google, this app displays “no time”.

data.name: SettingsWindow.Text42
data.value: Troubleshooting • access_denied: Check test users and the signed-in account. Ask your administrator about organization policy blocks. • Unverified app: Verify your own client name and account. Stop if unsure. • Connection error after login: Check Calendar ID, API enablement in the same project, and permissions. Step 3 grants access again; Step 4 only checks the connection. • External/Testing refresh tokens for this scope expire after 7 days. Use Step 3 to sign in again. • Steps 3 and 4 save all settings fields, including non-Google settings.
